content.text:
All four steps are done.

1. **Data view:** 'Kibana Sample Data Flights' (index `kibana_sample_data_flights`, id `d3d7af60-4c81-11e8-b3d7-01146121b73d`) has a time field of `timestamp`. It has 33 fields, including `Carrier`, `Cancelled`, `Dest`, `Origin`, `AvgTicketPrice` and `FlightDelay`.
2. **Dashboard:** 'S4-890960ba Flights' (id `df9e3a64-e7da-460d-a210-6e29f5461b6b`) has two panels on that data view. One is a line chart of flight count over time. The other is a bar chart of flight count by `Carrier`.
3. **Alert rule:** 'S4-890960ba Cancelled flights' (id `da0997a1-0fc1-4149-9191-ef9f00f9c952`) is an Elasticsearch query rule. It runs every minute and fires when more than 10 documents with `Cancelled: true` arrive in a 5-minute window. I created it with `enabled: true`, so I didn't need to enable it afterwards. It has no actions, so it won't notify anyone when it fires.
4. **Edit and read-back:** I set the carrier panel title to 'Flights by carrier' with a PUT and confirmed it in the response. I had already given the panel that title when I created it, so the edit didn't change anything. Reading the rule back shows `enabled: true`.
